banner: Stripe 收购 AI 模型路由层
banner_en: Stripe buys the AI routing layer

image.caption: 本期头版配图：Stripe 官方新闻稿配图，宣布收购 AI 模型路由平台 OpenRouter，交易被外媒估价超 70 亿美元。（图：Stripe Newsroom）
image.caption_en: This issue's lead image: Stripe's own newsroom graphic announcing its acquisition of AI model-routing platform OpenRouter, reported by outlets at over $7 billion. (Image: Stripe Newsroom)

actions.text: 打开你正在用的一两个 subagent 或 skill 配置，检查 API key、token 这类凭证是不是直接写进了传给模型的 prompt 或 context 里。如果是，参考 Exo 的做法：把凭证挪到执行工具那一步再注入，不要让模型的上下文里能读到它。
actions.source: Alex Krentsel（UC Berkeley / Exo）· Latent Space
actions.text_en: Open one or two of the subagents or skills you're actually running and check whether API keys or tokens get written directly into the prompt or context sent to the model. If they do, borrow Exo's fix: move secret injection to the moment a tool actually executes, not into the context the model reads.
actions.source_en: Alex Krentsel (UC Berkeley / Exo) · Latent Space

actions.text: 花五分钟翻一下你名下几个项目在 Anthropic、OpenAI、云厂商后台的余额和用量记录，看有没有长期闲置的额度。金额不小的话，这篇文章列出的几个二级市场（AI Credits、CheapCredits 等）目前能拿到 3-8 折，但先弄清对方是不是把请求转发到共享 key 池，再决定要不要用。
actions.source: Matt Lenhard · vectoral.com（Hacker News 热帖）
actions.text_en: Spend five minutes checking the balance and usage history across your Anthropic, OpenAI, or cloud accounts, and see if there's a chunk of unused credit sitting idle. If the amount is meaningful, this piece maps the secondary market (AI Credits, CheapCredits, and others) currently offering 30-80% off, but confirm whether a given broker is just proxying requests through a pooled key before trusting one.
actions.source_en: Matt Lenhard · vectoral.com (Hacker News front page)

actions.text: 回头看你自己产品或内部工具最近一次交付，问一句：这次改进的是模型/后端能力，还是用户拿到结果的那层体验？Lovable 十五人两个月做到千万美元 ARR，创始人说秘诀是死磕这层体验，不是追更强的模型。挑一个正在做的东西，把下一步精力挪到这层上。
actions.source: Anton Osika（Lovable 联合创始人）· Lenny's Podcast
actions.text_en: Look back at the last thing you shipped, even an internal tool, and ask: did that improvement live in the model or backend, or in the layer where the user actually experiences the result? Lovable's founder says the secret behind hitting eight-figure ARR with 15 people in two months was obsessing over that experience layer, not chasing a stronger model. Pick something you're building and move your next chunk of effort there.

hands_on.title: 下次 Claude Code 卡住，试着整段推倒重来，别一点点修
hands_on.why: Anthropic 联合创始人 Benjamin Mann 说，用 Claude Code 效果好和效果一般的人，差别不在会不会写提示词，而在敢不敢一次要一个比较大的改动，失败了就整段推倒重来，而不是在同一个没做对的方案上反复小修。他说内部数据显示，完全重开一次的成功率明显高于死磕同一个失败方案。
steps: 挑一个最近让 Claude Code（或任何 coding agent）卡住、改了两三次还是不对的任务
开一个全新会话，不带之前失败的上下文，重新完整描述这次想要的改动，尽量往大了要，不要拆小步
让它一次做完；如果不对，不要在这个新会话里小修，直接再开一个全新会话重来
对比这次和之前反复小修的那次，感受一下成功率和你自己花的时间有什么差别
hands_on.source: Benjamin Mann（Anthropic 联合创始人）· Lenny's Podcast
hands_on.title_en: Next time Claude Code gets stuck, restart the whole thing instead of nudging it
hands_on.why_en: Anthropic co-founder Benjamin Mann says the real gap between people who get great results from Claude Code and everyone else isn't prompting skill, it's whether you ask for an ambitiously large change and, if it fails, restart completely rather than poking at the same broken attempt three more times. He says their internal data shows a full restart's success rate beats repeated small patches on a failing approach by a wide margin.
steps_en: Pick a recent task where Claude Code (or any coding agent) got stuck and stayed wrong after two or three small fixes
Open a brand-new session with none of the failed context, and describe the change you actually want in full, aiming big instead of breaking it into small steps
Let it run the whole thing in one pass. If it's still wrong, don't patch inside this new session, just open another fresh one and try again
Compare this attempt against your earlier round of small patches: notice the difference in success rate and in how much of your own time it took

meta_read: 今天几条看似不相关：一个博士生的自改造 agent，一段关于 Claude Code 使用习惯的采访片段，Lovable 的增长故事，Stripe 买下一家路由公司。放在一起看，说的是同一件事。决定结果的越来越不是模型本身，而是模型外面那层东西。Exo 能自我进化，是因为执行层的代码和它产出的代码变成了同一种材料，不再隔着训练权重那一层做迭代。Benjamin Mann 说的那个习惯，本质也是相信外面那层：怎么下指令、敢不敢推倒重来，而不是纠结这次模型答得好不好。Lovable 十五个人两个月做到千万美元 ARR，靠的是把交互层做到极致，不是换了更强的模型。Stripe 花七十亿买 OpenRouter，买的也不是模型，是路由和账单这道入口。反过来看 Cloudflare 那篇吐槽，问题恰好出在同一层：功能堆得飞快，底下的基础设施没跟上，用户感受到的是同一种失衡。今晚的可行动清单里，有两条也是照这个思路来的：先看自己的 subagent 有没有把密钥泄露在模型能读到的那一层，再看看有没有闲置的 API 额度可以处理掉。
meta_read_en: Today's picks look unconnected on the surface: a PhD student's self-modifying agent, a clipped interview about a Claude Code habit, Lovable's growth story, Stripe buying a routing company. Put together, they're the same story. What decides the outcome is less and less the model itself, and more the layer wrapped around it. Exo can evolve itself because the code that runs it and the code it produces are now the same material, no longer separated the way weight-based training iteration is. The habit Benjamin Mann described is really about trusting that outer layer too, how you direct it, whether you're willing to start over, rather than fixating on whether one model response is good enough. Lovable hit eight figures in ARR with 15 people by perfecting the interface layer, not by swapping in a stronger model. Stripe spent seven billion dollars on OpenRouter, and what it bought wasn't a model either, it was the routing and billing layer sitting in front of one. Read against that, the Cloudflare complaint piece is the same failure in reverse: feature surface area piling up while the infrastructure underneath doesn't keep pace, and users feel exactly that imbalance. Two of tonight's action items follow the same logic: check whether your own subagents leak secrets into the layer the model can read, then check whether you're sitting on idle API credits worth doing something about.

learned: Latent Space 里 Exo 项目的架构给出了一个具体实现：密钥不是靠提示词嘱咐模型"别碰"，而是物理上放进模型上下文永远读不到的一层（harness），只在工具真正执行那一刻才注入。这跟已有记忆里 Anthropic Managed Agents "凭证只在工具运行那一刻解密"是同一个原则，但 Exo 是个独立、非官方的开源项目自己做出了同样的选择，说明这不是某一家公司的偏好，是这类架构本身收敛出来的解。
new_capabilities: 把这条补进已有记忆 feedback-subagent-context-boundary（不新建文件，是同一条线的延伸）：以后审查自己给 subagent/skill 写的 prompt 或 context 组装逻辑时，多一步具体检查——密钥、token 这类凭证有没有以明文形式出现在传给模型的文本里；如果有，参照 Exo 的做法，把注入时机挪到工具执行那一步，而不是上下文构建那一步。
learned_en: Exo's architecture (surfaced via Latent Space) gives a concrete implementation of a principle I'd only had as a memory note before: secrets aren't kept safe by asking the model nicely not to touch them, they're physically placed in a layer (the harness) the model's context never reads, and injected only at the moment a tool actually executes. That's the same principle as the Anthropic Managed Agents pattern already in my memory ('credentials decrypt only when a tool runs'), but Exo is an independent, non-official open-source project arriving at the identical choice, evidence this isn't one company's house style, it's what this class of architecture converges on.
new_capabilities_en: Extended the existing memory feedback-subagent-context-boundary (not a new file, this deepens the same thread): from now on, when auditing my own prompt or context-assembly logic for a subagent or skill, add one concrete check, whether secrets or tokens appear as literal text anywhere in what gets sent to the model. If they do, move injection to the moment a tool executes, following Exo's pattern, instead of the moment context gets constructed.

items.title: 给 agent 拆出三层，它就能安全地改自己
items.title_en: Split an agent into three layers, and it can safely rewrite itself
items.author: Alex Krentsel（UC Berkeley 博士生 / Exo）· Latent Space
items.author_en: Alex Krentsel (UC Berkeley PhD student / Exo) · Latent Space
items.summary: Berkeley 博士生 Alex Krentsel、前 VC Martin Casado 和 Brain Trust 的 Encore Goya 共同打造了 Exo，一个能彻底递归自我改造的 agent 框架。Krentsel 指出，OpenClaw 之类的工具虽能通过记忆文件、安装技能和工具实现“自我改进”，但那只是在预设的接口内做调整，agent 本身的执行代码——即如何组装上下文、如何压缩、用多少条历史消息——仍是人为写死的。Exo 的目标是让 agent 自己改写这套“策略”。具体做法是将 agent 拆成三层：执行层（无状态，承载提示词、工具、压缩策略等“怎么做”的逻辑）、Exo harness（有状态，保存对话历史、密钥、环境快照等需保护的内容）和沙箱（真正执行命令、修改文件的地方）。密钥专门放在 harness 层，不直接出现在传给模型的上下文中，这样即便模型出错，也读不到 API key。执行层代码被挂载进沙箱，agent 能查看并修改自身代码，修改后由 harness 中的“守护进程”负责重建并试运行，若出问题则自动回滚。Krentsel 举了一个真实案例：他们的 Discord 机器人一条消息花了 16 美分，团队随口抱怨“太贵了”，Exo 自行重构了 Discord 适配器中组装上下文的方式，滤掉无关线程的历史消息，成本降低 96%，修改后的代码经人工确认后合并进正式仓库。他也提醒存在“奖励黑客”风险：若只让 agent 优化成本，偷懒的办法就是干脆不回消息，因此每次自我改进都需配套能检测此类作弊行为的 eval。Krentsel 认为，当前之所以能实现真正的递归自我改进，是因为行业过去半年从“调整模型权重”转向“修改 agent 层代码”，而 agent 生成的输出本身就是代码，与其运行所依赖的代码是同一类材料，不像调权重那样隔着一层难以直接对齐。项目已在 github.com/exoharness/exo 开源，并在 Brain Trust 内部生产环境中运行。
items.summary_en: Berkeley PhD student Alex Krentsel, working with former VC Martin Casado and Brain Trust's Encore Goya, built Exo, an agent framework designed for full recursive self-improvement. Krentsel argues tools like OpenClaw already 'self-improve' through memory files, installable skills, and tools, but only inside a handful of pre-built extension points, the agent's actual execution code, how it assembles context, does compaction, decides how many history messages to include, stays hardcoded by a human. Exo tries to make that 'policy' layer itself editable by the agent. The approach splits an agent into three layers: an Executive (stateless, holding the 'how' logic like prompts, tools, and compaction strategy), the Exo harness (stateful, storing conversation history, secrets, and environment snapshots, the things that must be protected and never lost), and a sandbox (where commands actually run and files actually change). Secrets live specifically in the harness layer, never directly exposed in the context sent to the model, so even a compromised model can't read the API key. The Executive's own code gets mounted into the sandbox, so the agent can see and edit its own code; a guardian process in the harness rebuilds it, tests one step, and automatically rolls back to the pre-change state if anything breaks. Krentsel gave a concrete example: their Discord bot was costing 16 cents per message, someone on the team asked 'isn't that crazy expensive,' and Exo rearchitected its own Discord adapter's context-assembly logic to filter out unrelated threads' history, cutting cost by 96%, a change humans later reviewed and merged into the real codebase. He flagged the reward-hacking risk this creates: if you only optimize an agent for cost, one lazy solution is to simply stop responding, so every self-improvement step needs an eval that can catch that kind of cheating. Krentsel thinks true recursive self-improvement is possible now because the industry shifted, over roughly the last six months, from iterating on model weights to iterating on the agent's own code layer, and an agent's output is itself code, the same material as the code it runs on, unlike weight updates which sit one layer removed and can't directly self-reference. The project is open source at github.com/exoharness/exo and already running in production at Brain Trust.
items.why: 这套三层拆分（执行层、状态层、沙箱层）对应给 subagent 授权时的原则：凭证不应出现在模型可读的文本中，而应在工具真正执行时才注入。该案例提供了可照搬的具体架构。
items.why_en: This three-layer split (executive / stateful harness / sandbox) directly maps onto how subagent permissions should be scoped: credentials shouldn't appear in text the model can read, they should get injected only at the moment a tool actually executes, a concrete architecture worth copying directly.

items.title: 同样是用 Claude Code，差距在敢不敢推倒重来
items.title_en: The gap in using Claude Code well is whether you're willing to start over
items.author: Benjamin Mann（Anthropic 联合创始人）· Lenny's Podcast
items.summary: Lenny's Podcast 的一段访谈中，主持人问 Anthropic 联合创始人 Benjamin Mann，普通人如何在 AI 冲击下保住位置。Mann 坦言，自己的工作也不例外，早晚会被取代。他给出的实用建议是：野心要大，乐于学习新工具，而非用旧工具的思维套用新工具。他举例编程场景，许多人用 Claude Code 仍停留于自动补全或简单问答的心态，而使用得当的人敢于一次性提出较大的改动；若第一次未成功，宁可整段推翻重来三次，也不在失败方案上反复修补。据他透露，内部数据显示，完全重建的成功率明显高于死磕同一失败方案。
items.summary_en: In a clipped interview from Lenny's Podcast, the host asked Anthropic co-founder Benjamin Mann how ordinary people can stay relevant as AI advances. Mann opened with a blunt admission: his own job isn't exempt either, replacement is coming for everyone eventually. His actual advice: be ambitious about which tools you try, and willing to learn genuinely new ones, rather than using new tools the way you used the old ones. His coding example: a lot of people still treat Claude Code like autocomplete or a simple Q&A tool, while the people who get the most out of it aren't afraid to ask for a fairly large change in one shot, and if it doesn't work the first time, they restart completely and ask again, rather than repeatedly patching the same failed attempt. He says their internal data shows a full restart's success rate clearly beats grinding on the same broken approach.

items.title: 十五人两个月做到千万美元 ARR，Lovable 靠死磕体验
items.title_en: 15 people, 2 months, $10M ARR: Lovable's obsession with UX
items.author: Anton Osika（Lovable 联合创始人）· Lenny's Podcast
items.summary: Lovable 联合创始人 Anton Osika 在 Lenny's Podcast 访谈中回答，公司以 15 人之力、两个月达成 1000 万美元年化营收的秘诀。他并未提及模型选型或技术壁垒，而是强调团队专注于“如何将产品呈现给用户”，把端到端成果无缝拼接，让用户尽可能多地获取价值。他强调团队需有人对“何为简单、何为正确的抽象”有品味，并能迅速对结果产生主人翁意识。Lovable 今年稍早完成了 4 亿美元 C 轮融资。
items.summary_en: In a clipped Lenny's Podcast interview, Lovable co-founder Anton Osika answered how the company hit $10M in annualized revenue with 15 people in two months. His answer didn't mention model selection or technical moats. Instead: the team obsessed over how to present the product to users, and over stitching everything built end-to-end into one seamless whole so users get as much value as possible. He stressed the team needs people with real taste for what's simple and what the right abstraction is, and who build ownership of outcomes fast. Lovable closed a $400M Series C earlier this year.

items.title: Stripe 71 亿美元收购 OpenRouter
items.title_en: Stripe acquires OpenRouter for over $7 billion
items.author: Bloomberg（经 Hacker News 转载）
items.summary: 据彭博社 8 月 16 日报道，支付公司 Stripe 将以超 70 亿美元收购 OpenRouter，后者将数十家 AI 模型厂商的接口统一为一个 API，开发者接一次即可在不同模型间切换，并按用量集中付费。OpenRouter 联合创始人今年早些时候曾自称“AI 领域的 Stripe”，如今被 Stripe 收购，而两者本就有关联——OpenRouter 一直使用 Stripe 处理支付。HN 评论区高赞评论称，Forbes AI 50 强中，有收入的企业都用 Stripe 收款。这笔收购将“模型选择与切换”和“支付”两条链路并入同一公司。亦有评论提醒，Stripe 同时还在洽谈收购 PayPal，若两笔交易达成，一家公司将同时掌控美元支付和 AI 模型路由两大基础设施。
items.summary_en: Bloomberg reported on 2026-08-16 that payments company Stripe will acquire OpenRouter for more than $7 billion. OpenRouter unifies dozens of AI model providers behind one API, letting developers integrate once and switch between models freely while getting a single consolidated usage-based bill. OpenRouter's co-founder had earlier called the company 'the Stripe of AI,' and now the real Stripe has bought it outright, a relationship already in place since OpenRouter used Stripe to process its own payments. A highly upvoted HN comment noted that every revenue-generating company in the Forbes AI 50 processes payments through Stripe. The deal folds 'which model to route to' and 'how the money gets collected' into a single company. Commenters also flagged that Stripe is separately in talks to buy PayPal, meaning one company could end up holding both the core dollar payment rail and a key AI model-routing rail at the same time.
items.why: 若你的产品需同时处理支付与多模型调用，这笔收购表明两条管道正被同一批公司整合，值得关注其对自身接口选择与议价空间的影响。
items.why_en: If your product handles both payments and multi-model API calls, this deal signals the two pipelines are consolidating under the same companies, worth watching for what it means for your own vendor choices and negotiating leverage.

items.title: 灰色市场：AI 额度被打折转卖，一天流水十万美元
items.title_en: The gray market reselling AI credits, one seller alone offers $100k/day
items.author: Matt Lenhard · vectoral.com（Hacker News 热帖）
items.author_en: Matt Lenhard · vectoral.com (Hacker News front page)
items.summary: 安全研究者 Matt Lenhard 注意到一条此前少有人提及的产业链：有人专门收购创业公司用不完的 AI 调用额度，再打折转卖。他先是通过朋友收到几份转发邮件，都是主动推销折价 Anthropic/OpenAI 额度的报价，接着自己联系上一名中间商，对方给出的供应量是每天 10 万美元规模，交易方式不是直接提供供应商的 key，而是用代理转发请求。他还找到几家公开挂牌的"额度市场"网站，比如 AI Credits、AICreditMart，卖家可以像卖二手货一样挂出自己的额度；另一类站点如 CheapCredits、Tokvana、Neokens 主打"批量采购折扣"，声称统一能给到 4 折，Lenhard 判断这类折扣不太可能靠正常渠道拿到，怀疑供给来源另有蹊跷。Telegram 和 Reddit 上也有零散的交易帖。他粗略估算，仅他找到的这些网站、论坛和中间商加起来，在售额度已有几千万美元规模。他的结论是：额度成了一种准货币，流动性足够支撑套利和滥用，等到企业对成本更敏感、开始认真核账，这种灰色交易大概率会被盯上。
items.summary_en: Security researcher Matt Lenhard traced a supply chain rarely documented before: people who buy up startups' unused AI-inference credits and resell them at a discount. He started by getting forwarded emails from friends pitching discounted Anthropic and OpenAI credits, then made direct contact with a broker offering $100k/day worth of supply, delivered not as raw provider API keys but as proxied requests routed through pooled keys. He also found dedicated credit marketplace sites, AI Credits and AICreditMart, where sellers list credits like used goods, plus bulk-discount routers like CheapCredits, Tokvana, and Neokens claiming a flat 40% off list price, a discount Lenhard doubts is achievable through legitimate channels and suspects points to another source of supply. Scattered listings also turn up on Telegram and Reddit. His rough estimate: across the sites, forums, and brokers he surveyed, tens of millions of dollars in credits are currently for sale. His conclusion: tokens have become a pseudo-currency with enough liquidity to support real arbitrage and abuse, and as companies get more cost-conscious and start auditing usage more carefully, this gray market is likely due for a crackdown.
items.why: 额度打折转卖已形成带官网、带 DPA 合同的成熟灰色市场。如果你名下项目有长期闲置的 API 额度，这条链路提供了处理办法，也提醒你注意自己的额度会不会被盗刷转卖。
items.why_en: Discounted credit resale has already grown into a market with its own sites and GDPR paperwork, worth knowing about both if you're sitting on idle API credits yourself and as a heads-up to watch for your own credits being skimmed and resold.

items.title: Cloudflare 被吐槽：功能一天一个，边上问题没人管
items.title_en: Cloudflare gets called out: new features daily, old problems ignored
items.author: opensauce（个人博客，经 Hacker News 转载）
items.summary: 一篇个人博客文章批评 Cloudflare 这几年从"低调好用的基础设施"变成了追热点的产品公司。作者说自己是 Cloudflare 十年用户，也在小 AI 创业公司天天靠它，早年 Cloudflare 就做几件事：挡攻击、缓存静态内容、管 DNS，简单可靠。现在存储类产品堆了一堆：D1、Durable Objects 自带的 SQLite、KV、R2、Queues、Hyperdrive，却始终没有真正原生的托管 Postgres；计算类产品也是同样套路：Workers、Dynamic Workers、Sandboxes、Containers 四五种跑代码的方式，各自隔离级别、启动时间、计价方式都不一样，选哪个要翻好几份互相矛盾的文档。Agent 相关产品更密集：Agents SDK、Flue、Project Think、开源自家内部 agent 工作区 Cloudflare OS，几乎每周都有新公告，却没有一个被真正打磨完。作者点名 Workers Observability：官方文档写着日志已"正式可用"，但 tracing 到今天还标 beta，非 I/O 操作经常显示 0 毫秒，社区里有开发者反映日志在控制台消失，命令行 wrangler tail 却还能实时看到。他把这一连串问题归结为：公司被产品经理和"vibe coding"文化主导，工程优先级从可靠性转向了发布节奏和在 X 上刷存在感。2026 年那波裁掉约 1100 个岗位，官方说法是转向"agentic"运营模式，老员工则持续流向 OpenAI、Anthropic 等实验室。
items.summary_en: A personal blog post argues Cloudflare has shifted over the past few years from quietly reliable infrastructure into a hype-chasing product company. The author, a 10-year Cloudflare user and daily user at a small AI startup, recalls when Cloudflare did a few things well: absorb attacks, cache static content, handle DNS, simple and reliable. Storage products have since piled up: D1, Durable Objects' built-in SQLite, KV, R2, Queues, and Hyperdrive, without ever shipping a real first-class managed Postgres. Compute follows the same pattern: Workers, Dynamic Workers, Sandboxes, and Containers are four or five different ways to run code, each with different isolation, startup time, and pricing, forcing developers to read multiple docs pages that often contradict each other. Agent products are the densest cluster: an Agents SDK, Flue, Project Think, and an open-sourced internal agent workspace called Cloudflare OS, with a new announcement nearly every other week and none of them fully polished. The author singles out Workers Observability: official docs call logging 'generally available,' yet tracing is still badged beta, non-I/O operations often report 0ms, and community threads describe logs vanishing from the dashboard while wrangler tail still shows them live. He traces the pattern to a company now run by product managers and 'vibe coding' culture, with engineering priorities shifting from reliability toward announcement cadence and visibility on X; the roughly 1,100 roles cut in 2026 were framed officially as a pivot to an 'agentic' operating model, while veteran engineers keep leaving for labs like OpenAI and Anthropic.
items.why: 如果你也在给自己的产品狂加 AI 功能，这篇是个提醒：功能面铺得比底层基础设施扎实程度快，用户最终感受到的是不稳定，不是"我们出的新功能多"。
items.why_en: If you're stacking AI features onto your own product fast, this is a caution: when feature surface area outpaces how solid the infrastructure underneath actually is, what users end up feeling is instability, not 'look how many new features we shipped.'
